title: Meeting Report Payload
description: Canonical, lossless structured model for a Decidero meeting report. This payload is the single source of truth: the JSON export is this object verbatim, and every human-facing rendering (Markdown, DOCX, the tabular CSV slice, the on-screen preview) is a pure function of it. Produced by the generic `report` activity (Layer 1) from upstream output bundles, finalized as that activity's output bundle, and re-rendered on demand from the stored model rather than recomputed. Method-specific shaping (which bundle feeds which section, which columns) lives in Layer-2 orchestration config, never in the activity.

report_version.description: Schema/contract version of this report payload, so downstream tools can depend on the shape.

title.description: Human title for the report. Defaults to the meeting title when absent.

meeting.description: Identifying context for the meeting the report summarizes.

method.description: Orchestration method name + version when the meeting was method-driven (e.g. Classical Delphi 1.0). Absent for ordinary linear meetings.

round_count.description: Number of materialized rounds for iterate-based methods; null/absent otherwise.

generated_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the report model was produced.

generated_by.description: Who/what produced the report (facilitator user id, or an engine/system marker).

sections.description: Ordered report body. Each section carries a generic, renderer-known type so all output formats render from the same shapes. Method-specific meaning is expressed by choosing/configuring these generic sections in Layer-2, not by adding method-specific section types.

metadata.description: Open extension slot (mirrors the bundle payload's metadata slot). Reserved for non-rendered provenance/diagnostics.

source.description: Provenance for a section: which upstream bundle/activity it was derived from. Mirrors the bundle payload source block so reports stay traceable to their inputs.

type.description: Generic section kind. Renderers switch on this. CSV export covers only the tabular kinds (`table`, `ranked_list`, and a `chart`'s underlying series). A `chart` stores its data series in the canonical model; renderers draw it (matplotlib PNG for DOCX/HTML) and always emit the underlying series as a table alongside.

body.description: Section payload; shape is governed by `type` via the allOf below.

body_narrative.description: Prose. `markdown` is the canonical text; renderers may downgrade to plain text. May carry an AI-drafted flag when produced by an ai-decision synthesis step (facilitator-confirmed before publish).

body_key_value.description: Flat list of labeled values (summary statistics, run parameters).

body_table.description: Generic tabular data. The CSV export serializes these directly.

body_ranked_list.description: Ordered list of items with optional per-item statistics. The Delphi converged list (rank + median + IQR + agreement band) is this shape. CSV-exportable.

stats.description: Optional per-item statistics (e.g. median, iqr, dispersion, agreement_band).

body_comment_thread.description: Grouped, peer-anonymous comments (e.g. cross-round Delphi feedback). Identity is never persisted here; `mine` is computed per-viewer at render time and is NOT part of the canonical model.

body_rounds.description: Round-by-round trace for iterate-based methods (the convergence story). Each round references the generic section shapes for its own body.

sections.description: Nested generic sections scoped to this round (e.g. the round's ranked_list).

body_chart.description: Chart as data, not pixels: the canonical model stores the series; renderers draw it (matplotlib PNG for DOCX/HTML) and also emit the series as a table. Standard report charts: a convergence curve (line: median IQR and/or Kendall's W per round), a rank-trajectory bump chart (one series per idea, y=rank with invert=true), and an agreement-band stacked bar (green/yellow/red counts per round).

categories.description: Ordered x positions, e.g. round labels ["Round 1", "Round 2", ...]. Series point arrays align to this length.

invert.description: Render with the axis inverted (rank 1 at top). Used by the rank-trajectory bump chart.

points.description: Values aligned to x_axis.categories; null = no datum for that x (e.g. item absent that round).
